title: False Friends and Rhetorical Connectors
summary: Avoid sophisticated false friends and use high-level connectors to build nuanced argumentation.

sections.heading: False friends that affect precision
sections.body: Some cognates look familiar but carry different meanings or registers. At C2, the goal is not only avoiding mistranslation but choosing the word that fits the argument.

examples.pt: Na verdade, o problema é outro.
examples.en: Actually/In fact, the problem is another one.
He intends to do a master's degree.

sections.heading: Advanced argumentative connectors
sections.body: Connectors such as **não obstante**, **a despeito de**, **conquanto**, **por conseguinte**, and **destarte** belong to formal writing. Use them accurately and sparingly.

examples.pt: Não obstante as críticas, a medida foi aprovada.
examples.en: Notwithstanding the criticism, the measure was approved.

examples.pt: A despeito do atraso, o evento foi bem recebido.
examples.en: Despite the delay, the event was well received.

examples.pt: Os dados são inconsistentes; por conseguinte, a conclusão é frágil.
examples.en: The data are inconsistent; consequently, the conclusion is weak.

sections.heading: Rhetorical framing
sections.body: High-level Portuguese often frames arguments with expressions that guide interpretation: **cumpre destacar**, **convém observar**, **não se pode perder de vista**, **à primeira vista**.

examples.pt: Cumpre destacar que a decisão não foi unânime.
examples.en: It should be noted that the decision was not unanimous.

examples.pt: Convém observar que os números são preliminares.
examples.en: It is worth noting that the numbers are preliminary.

examples.pt: À primeira vista, a solução parece simples.
examples.en: At first glance, the solution seems simple.

keyPoints: False friends can distort both meaning and tone.
Atualmente means currently; na verdade often means actually/in fact.
Formal connectors should match the logic of the sentence precisely.
Rhetorical frames help readers understand the role of each claim.

commonMistakes.note: Pretender means intend; fingir means pretend.

commonMistakes.right: Use então/por isso in casual conversation; reserve destarte for very formal style.
commonMistakes.note: Destarte is highly formal and rare.
